account:
Today repeated rumours have circulated about a bridge or port change supposedly discussed at the bakery. Several townsfolk repeated nearly identical vague wording. One report named baker, freight, innkeeper and neighbour as present, but I have not personally witnessed such a discussion or learned any actual proposal, purpose, or decision. At tea, neighbour said they visited the bakery this morning but did not personally hear a crossing discussion and could not confirm or attribute a proposal. They reported no urgent river concerns. I cannot yet tell whether the rumour reflects real business or merely repetition.

The ten o'clock mill grain inspection was already unconfirmed. I attended but found no responsible staff or records. The stall contained seventy-six hay bales and 104 emeralds; that is not a full stock audit or evidence of wrongdoing. A townsfolk report said innkeeper carried hay block at the mill, but I do not know why. I asked secretary to record the inspection's limitations, identify a responsible mill contact, arrange a confirmed inspection, and seek firsthand information from baker. No council letters or reliable crossing details had reached secretary earlier today.

I kept the fifteen o'clock tea visit but stayed too long talking and reached my office at seventeen, late for the sixteen-thirty appointment. Secretary is here; I have not yet received their follow-up. Neighbour may meet me at town hall at eighteen for a walk if business permits. I should hear secretary's report before forming any conclusion about the rumours.
